note: Adjudicated accidental and house-orthography variants. The witnesses agree on the substantive text.

adjudicated.ruling: This edition accents capitals, by the house rule in ORTHOGRAPHY.md, because the accent tells a reader where the stress falls and a capital does not stop being a syllable. Most printings omit them; the reading is identical.
The lexical accent is restored in the working text under the edition's house convention; the witness's capital typography is recorded exactly.

The j-form against this edition's i-form, by the house rule in ORTHOGRAPHY.md. This edition prints i because the books it edits do: the approved 1962 Benziger printing sets Iesu, Ioánnem, iube and maiestátis throughout, and so does the Ordo Missae of Pallottinum, Poznań 1963, which is the book a Polish reader is most likely to hold. The mid-century hand missals print j; neither spelling is a different word, and the apparatus records theirs.

The approved Benziger printing ends the respond with a full stop after móritur, before the verse ℣. Sed (p. 26). The pinned digital reading's comma, where its source line ends before the verse, is recorded exactly; the words are the same.
